text.p: Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in Budapest-listed Cofinec S.A. packaging company are undervalued therefore mean a buying opportunity, Nomura Equity Research said in a company update.

"Although Cofinec's share price has recovered somewhat from its low point...it still remains very depressed," Nomura's analysts Frances Cloud and Matthew Arnold said in a report, dated April 15 and obtained by Reuters on Tuesday.
"We believe that this may not be justified."
Cofinec, a French-registered company with operations in Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, reached its 1997 low on January 6 at 4,650 forints. On Monday it closed at 5,000.
On the SEAQ Cofinec GDRs opened at $28.75 and 0829 GMT it was marked at $28.25.
Cofinec, after a successful flotation in mid-1996, surprised the market by reporting very poor H1 figures.

"The source of Cofinec's difficulties was a sudden increase in competition on the Hungarian market, exacerbated by a lack of financial controls at Head Office which allowed the problem to go unnoticed for far too long," the analysts said.

The company has tackled the problem since and although it will take time to implement all the necessary changes, Nomura's analysts said the management was making the right moves and that earnings would show a strong recovery this year.
"This should restore confidence in the company and allow the share price to move decisively back over the $30 level," the analysts said. At the current level we recommend purchase."
